title: Casts of a decimal and a datetime to a string
verdict: the scale's digits with a leading zero; datetimes always print six fraction digits
description: A Decimal(p, s) casts to its integer part (at least one digit), a `.` and s fraction digits, with `-` for a negative (`10.50`, `-0.05`, `0.00`, scale 0 `12`). When precision equals scale the integer part is `0` (`-0.500`), where DuckDB prints `-.500`.
A Datetime(us) casts to `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff` with all six fraction digits, also when they are zero (`2024-01-05 09:30:00.000000`, `…00.250000`), where DuckDB and Spark trim trailing zeros.
reference: Open (#346): a reference text for decimals and timestamps is not decided; this records what Polars gives.

evidence.sql: pl.Decimal(3, 3) of -0.5 and 0.5, pl.Decimal(4, 2) of 0.05, pl.Decimal(10, 0) of 12, cast to pl.String

provenance.notes: Re-run under `collect(engine="streaming")` on the decimals (`10.50`, `-0.05`, `0.00`, `-0.500`, `0.500`, `0.05`, `12`) and read by reviewer 2 on the datetimes: the same text.
